chapters.title: Chapter 2: Who Needs to Pay Advance Tax

lessons.title: Investors and Traders: Capital Gains, Dividends and F&O Income

body.text: Market income is the single biggest reason ordinary salaried Indians become advance taxpayers. Capital gains carry no TDS at all, dividends carry TDS at only 10%, and F&O profits are business income with no TDS. If you invest or trade through Zerodha, Groww or Upstox, your broker is not paying your tax for you.

children.text: India now has more than 20 crore demat accounts, and a large share of them belong to people whose main income is a salary. Every time one of them books a profit on NSE or BSE, a small tax liability appears that no employer or bank has deducted. This lesson shows how each type of market income is taxed, when it pushes you over ₹10,000, and one relief that makes timing easier.

children.text: The same ₹5 lakh can cost ₹48,750 or ₹1,56,000 depending on what kind of income it is. For advance tax, all three are well over the ₹10,000 line, and none of them has TDS deducted.

body.title: Quick Check: Which Rate Applies?
body.question: Priyanka bought units of a debt mutual fund in June 2024 and redeemed them in August 2026 for a gain of ₹90,000. Her salary puts her in the 30% slab. How is the gain taxed?
options: 12.5% as long-term capital gains, because she held the units for more than two years
At her 30% slab rate, because debt funds bought after 1 April 2023 are taxed at slab rates regardless of holding period
It is tax-free, because it is below ₹1.25 lakh
body.explanation: Gains on debt mutual funds bought on or after 1 April 2023 are taxed at slab rates whatever the holding period, and the ₹1.25 lakh exemption applies only to long-term gains on listed equity shares and equity-oriented funds. At 30% plus cess, her ₹90,000 gain creates ₹28,080 of tax with no TDS, enough on its own to trigger advance tax.

children.text: Capital Gains: The Salaried Investor's Blind Spot

Karan is a salaried project manager in Hyderabad with his salary TDS fully in order. This year he sells Infosys shares he has held for four years, and some HDFC Bank shares he bought eight months ago.

body.title: Show me the math: Karan's capital gains tax

children.text: Because his salary uses up his basic exemption limit, none of it is available to reduce the short-term gain. And the rebate cannot be used against tax on either gain.

body.label: Karan's uncovered tax from two share sales
body.context: No TDS on either sale. Well over ₹10,000, so he is liable for advance tax even though he never thinks of himself as a trader.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The LTCG Exemption
body.textWithBlank: Long-term capital gains on listed equity shares and equity-oriented mutual funds are tax-free up to ₹___ in a tax year.
body.explanation: The annual exemption is ₹1,25,000, and only gains above it are taxed at 12.5%. It is one limit per person per year across all such gains, not ₹1.25 lakh per stock or per fund.

children.text: Dividends: TDS at 10%, Tax at Your Slab

Dividends feel passive and safe, and many investors assume the TDS already deducted settles them. For anyone in the 20% or 30% slab, it does not. Lakshmi, a Coimbatore-based doctor employed by a hospital, holds a portfolio of high-dividend PSU and FMCG stocks.

body.title: Try It: Lakshmi's Dividend Gap
body.prompt: Lakshmi's salary is taxed at the 30% slab and her employer's TDS covers it fully. Her dividends total ₹2,00,000, with TDS of ₹20,000 already deducted. Including 4% cess, how much tax on the dividends is still due? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: Tax on ₹2,00,000 at 30% is ₹60,000, and with 4% cess it is ₹62,400. Subtracting ₹20,000 of TDS leaves ₹42,400. The 10% TDS rate was designed as a floor, not a final tax, so higher-slab dividend investors almost always owe more.

children.text: F&O and Intraday Trading: Business Income

markDefs.definition: Income from a business activity, including F&O trading on a recognised exchange, taxed at slab rates. Expenses directly related to trading can be deducted, and losses can be set off against most other income except salary.
Income from trades squared off on the same day without delivery, such as intraday equity. Taxed at slab rates, and losses can only be set off against speculative gains.

body.text: Business losses from F&O can reduce other income in the same year, except salary. A salaried investor with a ₹3,00,000 long-term gain and a ₹2,00,000 F&O loss has a net gain of ₹1,00,000, which falls inside the ₹1.25 lakh exemption, so tax on the gain drops from ₹22,750 to nil. When estimating advance tax, look at your whole year across segments, not each one separately.

children.text: One Relief That Makes Timing Easier

You cannot predict a capital gain in June if you only decide to sell in January. The law recognises this. If the shortfall in an earlier instalment is because of capital gains or dividends that arose after that instalment's due date, no interest is charged for the missed instalment, provided you pay the tax on that income in the remaining instalments, or by 31 March if none are left. This relief carries over from the proviso to old section 234C into section 425.

body.title: Scenario: Ritu's January Sale
body.scenario: Ritu, a salaried architect in Kochi with fully covered salary TDS, had no market income until 22 January 2027. That day she sells shares she bought in September 2026 for a short-term gain of ₹3,00,000. She paid no advance tax in June, September or December because she had nothing to pay it on.
body.prompt: Is she already in default for the first three instalments? How much should she pay, and by when, to avoid interest?
body.modelAnswer: She is not in default for June, September or December, because the gain did not exist on those dates. Tax on the short-term gain is 20% of ₹3,00,000, which is ₹60,000, or ₹62,400 with 4% cess. Since the next and last instalment is 15 March 2027, she should pay the full ₹62,400 as advance tax by that date. If she does, the relief for capital gains means no interest for the earlier instalments. If she waits until she files her return, she loses that relief and pays interest for not paying advance tax as well. A simple rule for investors: whenever you book a meaningful gain, check your Zerodha Console or broker tax P&L the same week and pay the tax by the next due date.

body.text: The timing relief applies to income that genuinely arose after an instalment date. It does not help with F&O profits, which build up through the year as business income, or with gains you had already booked but forgot to include. Treat your trading P&L like a freelancer's invoices and estimate each quarter.

body.title: Before Each Advance Tax Due Date
steps: Download the tax P&L report from your broker, such as Zerodha Console, for the tax year so far
Separate short-term gains, long-term gains, F&O profit or loss, and intraday profit or loss
Check AIS for dividends and the TDS deducted on them
Estimate the tax on each type at its correct rate, netting eligible F&O losses against other non-salary income
Add any debt mutual fund redemptions at your slab rate
If the uncovered total is ₹10,000 or more, pay up to the cumulative percentage due by that date, including tax on any new gains since the last instalment

body.label: Zerodha Console
body.description: Zerodha's back-office portal. The Tax P&L report splits realised gains into short-term, long-term, intraday and F&O for any date range, which is what you need for a quarterly advance tax estimate.

cards.definition: Gain on listed shares or equity funds held 12 months or less. Taxed at 20% under section 196 (old 111A). No TDS.
Gain on listed shares or equity funds held over 12 months. Taxed at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh a year under section 198 (old 112A). No TDS.
Gains on debt mutual funds bought on or after 1 April 2023 are taxed at slab rates regardless of holding period.
10% deducted when one company pays you more than ₹10,000 in a year. Final tax is at your slab rate.
Non-speculative business income taxed at slab rates, with no TDS. Losses can offset other income except salary.
Speculative business income at slab rates. Losses can only be set off against speculative gains.

cards.term: Capital gains and dividend timing relief
cards.definition: No interest for earlier missed instalments if tax on capital gains or dividends arising later is paid in the remaining instalments or by 31 March.

points: Capital gains and F&O profits have no TDS for resident individuals, so the tax on them is fully uncovered
Short-term equity gains are taxed at 20%, long-term at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh, and debt fund gains bought after 1 April 2023 at slab rates
Dividends carry only 10% TDS, so investors in the 20% or 30% slab usually owe more
F&O and intraday profits are business income at slab rates, and F&O losses can reduce other non-salary income in the same year
Tax on capital gains or dividends that arise after an instalment date can be paid in the remaining instalments without interest for the earlier ones
Check your broker's tax P&L before each due date and pay tax on new gains promptly
